title: Where is Latin America's next upstream opportunity? | Wood Mackenzie
gist: A thin, largely promotional Wood Mackenzie piece framing Latin America (Brazil, Argentina, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela) as entering a new upstream oil and gas growth phase, but the substantive analysis is confined to an embedded 5:36 video rather than the article text itself.

insights.claim: Latin America is entering a new growth phase for upstream oil and gas investment, spanning Brazil's deepwater potential, Argentina's investment wave, and emerging opportunities in Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela.
insights.speaker: Pietro Ferreira
insights.so_what: Investors screening for upstream E&P opportunities should track these five Latin American markets as a connected regional growth theme rather than isolated single-country plays.
insights.quote: From Brazil's deepwater potential to Argentina's investment wave and emerging opportunities in Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela, the region is entering a new phase of growth.

insights.claim: In Latin America's upstream sector, established producers are simultaneously expanding output, frontier exploration plays continue to attract investor attention, and regulatory changes are reshaping the investment landscape.
insights.speaker: Pietro Ferreira
insights.so_what: Points to a three-pronged dynamic (production growth, frontier exploration, regulatory shifts) investors should monitor together rather than relying on a single catalyst to time the region.
insights.quote: Established producers are expanding output, frontier plays continue to attract attention, and regulatory changes are reshaping the investment landscape.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's substantive commentary on which Latin American upstream projects are drawing the biggest investment and which commercial and policy forces will define the region's next growth wave is delivered via an embedded 5-minute-36-second video featuring analysts Pietro Ferreira and Adrian Lara, not reproduced in the article's own text.
insights.speaker: Pietro Ferreira
insights.so_what: The actionable specifics live in the video, not this text, so investors relying only on the written article will miss the real analysis and should watch the video directly.
insights.locator: In this video, Wood Mackenzie experts

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie analyst Adrian Lara published analysis in January 2026 on how Venezuela's regime change affects oil production and crude and product markets, indicating the firm treats Venezuela's political transition as a live driver of Latin American oil market dynamics.
insights.speaker: Adrian Lara
insights.so_what: Flags Venezuela's post-regime-change oil sector as a distinct, actively-tracked catalyst for crude and product markets that investors should follow via Wood Mackenzie's dedicated coverage.
insights.quote: Venezuela regime change: what it means for oil production, crude and product markets
insights.locator: Venezuela regime change: what it means

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie analyst Pietro Ferreira has drawn a comparison between Argentina's giant shale play and the Midland Basin, suggesting the firm is positioning Argentina's shale resource as a potentially world-class unconventional play.
insights.speaker: Pietro Ferreira
insights.so_what: A Midland Basin comparison implies scale and economics that investors evaluating Argentine shale opportunities should benchmark against.
insights.quote: Is Argentina's giant shale play the next Midland Basin?
insights.locator: Is Argentina's giant shale play the next Midland Basin?

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie has maintained ongoing coverage of how Argentine President Milei's policies affect the country's oil and gas sector, alongside broader analysis of the challenges facing gas resource development across Latin America.
insights.speaker: Adrian Lara
insights.so_what: Indicates Argentine policy risk/reform under Milei and regional gas development constraints are recurring watch items in Wood Mackenzie's Latin America upstream coverage.
insights.locator: What does Milei mean for oil and gas in Argentina?
